story.title: Sen. Cassidy Supports Todd Blanche's Attorney General Confirmation
story.summary: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy has announced his support for Todd Blanche's nomination as attorney general, which is expected to facilitate Blanche's confirmation by the Senate. Cassidy's backing comes after two other Republican senators expressed their opposition to Blanche's nomination, making Cassidy's support crucial for moving forward.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in Blanche's path?
explore_lenses.title: Cassidy supplied the pivotal expected vote
explore_lenses.summary: Cassidy's endorsement did not erase the objections to Blanche; it changed the expected vote count after two Republicans announced opposition and Sen. Mitch McConnell remained absent.

claims.text: Cassidy said he would vote for Blanche despite calling Blanche's approval of the proposed fund and tax-audit protections poor judgment; he said he preferred Blanche to another acting attorney general.

Collins and Murkowski had announced opposition, while CBS reported that all Senate Democrats were expected to vote no; with McConnell absent, Cassidy's support left Blanche positioned to lose only those two Republicans and still prevail.
The Senate Judiciary Committee had already advanced the nomination 12-10 on August 4 after Cornyn and Tillis backed it.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Expected Democratic votes and McConnell's attendance could still affect the final margin.

explore_lenses.label: What do supporters and critics argue?
explore_lenses.title: The fund order is the central dispute
explore_lenses.summary: Supporters point to Blanche's written rescission of the proposed compensation fund and limits on the tax provision; critics argue those actions do not permanently prevent a future administration decision or enforce the underlying settlement's changes.

claims.text: Blanche's order said no fund had operated: no members were appointed, funds transferred, claims process created, or claims paid; it also said the tax-audit provision applies retroactively to open claims at the time of settlement rather than future filings.
Cornyn and Tillis said the formal order and clarification addressed their concerns, while Cornyn said the department needed a stabilizing, confirmed leader.

Murkowski said confirmation would remove Senate leverage over the fund; Durbin and a former Justice Department lawyer argued that an executive order could be reversed and that the settlement itself was not modified by the order.
Collins cited the proposed fund and other Justice Department actions that she said had made the department increasingly political.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next procedurally?
explore_lenses.title: A cloture motion is pending; timing is open
explore_lenses.summary: The nomination has cleared committee and is on the Senate floor track, but the available Senate record as of August 7 shows no cloture vote result or final confirmation vote.

claims.text: Senate records list Majority Leader John Thune's August 5 cloture motion on PN1078, Todd Blanche's nomination, with no vote result recorded through August 7.
The Senate's official materials state that a simple majority can invoke cloture on nominations and that confirmation requires majority support.

CBS forecast that Cassidy's support makes Blanche likely to be confirmed, but reported that it was unclear whether the Senate would hold the confirmation vote before its planned five-week recess because accelerating the process would require Democratic consent.

story_report.summary: Sen. Bill Cassidy said he will vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general, giving the nomination a crucial boost after Republican Sens. Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski announced their opposition. CBS reported that Senate Democrats were expected to vote against Blanche and that Sen. Mitch McConnell was absent, a count under which Cassidy’s support would leave Blanche able to lose the two Republican votes and still prevail. No final Senate vote had been recorded as of Aug. 7.

sections.heading: Fund Order Drives Confirmation Debate
sections.body: Cassidy said he preferred Blanche to another acting attorney general, while also describing Blanche’s approval of a proposed fund and tax-audit protections as poor judgment. Blanche’s order stated that no fund had operated: no members had been appointed, money transferred, claims process created or claims paid. It also said the tax-audit provision covered open claims at the time of settlement, not future filings. Murkowski, however, said confirmation would remove Senate leverage over the fund, while others argued an executive order could be reversed and did not modify the settlement itself.

sections.heading: Senate Process Remains Incomplete
sections.body: The Senate Judiciary Committee advanced Blanche’s nomination 12-10 on Aug. 4 after Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis supported it; both said the formal order and clarification addressed their concerns. Senate records list Majority Leader John Thune’s Aug. 5 cloture motion on Blanche’s nomination, but no result was recorded through Aug. 7. A simple majority can invoke cloture on nominations and confirm a nominee, though CBS reported that an expedited vote before the planned five-week recess would require Democratic consent.

unresolved.text: No final vote date or confirmation outcome was documented in the consulted Senate record as of Aug. 7, and McConnell’s attendance and Democratic voting could affect the final margin.
Whether the fund or other settlement provisions could later be revived or enforced remains contested.

related_stories.title: Trump Plans Supreme Court Appeal After Court Halts White House Ballroom Construction
related_stories.summary: A federal appeals court has blocked President Trump's $400 million ballroom construction project at the White House, ruling that he cannot proceed without congressional approval. The court's decision affirms a lower court ruling and allows only below-ground construction to continue. Trump has announced his intention to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court, calling it unjust.

related_stories.title: Senate Approves Bipartisan Sanctions Bill Targeting Russia and Iran
related_stories.summary: The Senate has passed a bipartisan bill imposing stricter sanctions on Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran. The legislation, which received an overwhelming vote of 86-11, was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, whose recent death expedited its passage. The bill aims to penalize countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas, aiming to reduce revenue for Russia amid ongoing conflicts.

related_stories.title: Trump Resumes Efforts to Dismiss Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
related_stories.summary: Donald Trump is renewing his attempts to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook after the US Supreme Court previously blocked his efforts. The administration is moving forward with the dismissal despite Cook's denial of mortgage fraud allegations that prompted the initial attempt to terminate her position.
